abstract.text: A small HTTP/1.1 server for apps and tools: routing, files, forms, uploads and WebSockets, without dependencies.
Six small programs that show how the pieces fit together, and that you can run.
Add NanoHTTP to a project, answer your first request and learn where to go next.
Look at every request before it is routed, and replace parts of the server by subclassing.

An HTTP request: method, path, query, headers and body, plus the address of the client
and the variables of the route that matched. The server creates one for every request
and hands it to middleware and handlers. A request is a reference type, compared and
hashed by identity.

A function that answers a request. It runs on the thread of the connection that sent
the request, one request at a time per connection, and many handlers run at the same
time for different connections (unless the server has only one thread). A handler may
block (a slow handler delays only its own connection) but must protect state that it
shares with other handlers.
